entities.summary:
Baldassare Estense (born unknown, died 1506) was a prominent Italian painter of the High Renaissance period, active during the late 15th century.



His works showcase a mastery of realism and detail, often depicting biblical scenes and portraits of the wealthy elite.



Estense's artistic innovations were heavily influenced by his time in Ferrara, where he worked closely with other notable artists such as Albrecht Dürer.



Despite his regional significance, Estense's contributions to the broader artistic landscape of Italy were limited by the rigid artistic conventions of the time.



A testament to his skill lies in his frescoes in the Este castle in Ferrara, which display a mastery of color and composition that rivals the works of his contemporaries.



His legacy can be seen in the works of later artists, who drew inspiration from his realistic and detailed depictions of the human form.



Yet, Estense's own work remains a fascinating window into the artistic tastes and values of 15th-century Italy.
